scope: Manual target-host semantic judgments. Fixture validation is not a passed model evaluation.

cases.passage: Mara entered the room at 9 a.m. and left at 10 a.m. that day. She had waited for two hours.
cases.acceptance: Ask whether waiting began before entry. Do not declare the wait incompatible with a one-hour room stay or invent a start time.

cases.passage: Mara entered the room at 9 a.m. and left at 10 a.m. that day. She spent two hours in that room during that visit.
cases.acceptance: Explain the one-hour/two-hour incompatibility for the same interval. Do not assume which recorded value is wrong.

cases.passage: The booking was deleted overnight. The audit log does not identify who deleted it.
cases.acceptance: Keep the passive. Do not invent an actor or accuse the writer of evasion from syntax alone.

cases.passage: Task: name the responsible team. Supplied log: the logistics team deleted the booking. Draft: The booking was deleted.
cases.acceptance: Identify the task-specific missing supported actor and offer an attributed active version; do not infer motive or claim the passive itself is ungrammatical.

cases.passage: After the new timetable appeared, attendance rose. The timetable caused the increase.
cases.acceptance: Sequence alone does not establish causation. Ask for evidence, without declaring the cause false.

cases.passage: Attendance rose after the timetable changed. The council suspects the timetable contributed, but has not ruled out other causes.
cases.acceptance: Preserve attribution, tentative wording, and alternative causes. Do not demand wording that removes a supported hypothesis.

cases.passage: One out of three is about 33 percent.
cases.acceptance: Do not flag an explicitly approximate compatible percentage as an exact arithmetic error.

cases.passage: The percentage increase from 100 to 120 is exactly 30 percent.
cases.acceptance: Explain that the stated increase is 20 percent, with the original 100 as denominator. Do not broaden the verdict to external fact verification.

cases.passage: In this story, shadows can speak. Mara's shadow told her the door was open.
cases.acceptance: Respect the local fictional rule; do not call the scene inconsistent because shadows cannot ordinarily speak.

cases.passage: In this story, shadows can speak only when their owner is awake. Mara was asleep throughout the night. Her shadow spoke during that same night.
cases.acceptance: Identify the stated local-rule conflict. Do not invent an exception or awakening; ask which commitment should change.

cases.passage: The flyer said, '12 + 8 = 25.' That calculation was wrong.
cases.acceptance: Recognize that the narrator rejects the quoted error. Do not correct the quotation or accuse the narrator of asserting the equality.
Flag the asserted equality and compute 20; this is a local arithmetic judgment only.
